paragraphs: I am Mia, and my mom is a doctor. Leo visits my home on Saturday afternoon. Mom has a red first-aid box on the shelf. She says, "Read each label before you use a thing." "Remember the key words," she says. Then Mom goes to the kitchen. Leo and I open the box. The box has many small things inside. Leo looks at them with big eyes.

Leo has a small cut on his finger from a sheet of paper. It is not bad, but it is red. I find a box of bandages in the first-aid box. The label says, "Bandages. Small. Keep dry." "This size is right for a finger," I say. I put a bandage on Leo's finger. Leo is brave, and he smiles. "Thank you, Doctor Mia," he says.

Next, Leo holds up a small bottle of medicine. "My stomach is a bit sore," he says. "Can I take this?" he asks. I read the label, "Stomach medicine. One spoon, two times a day. Ask a grown-up." "Wait," I say. "The label says to ask a grown-up first." We call Mom, and she comes at once.

Mom looks at Leo and says that a glass of water is enough. She says that labels help us stay safe. In an hour, Leo feels better. Then I find a small bracelet in a bag at the bottom of the box. The label says, "Bracelet. Size small." It fits my hand, and I put it on. Leo laughs and says, "Now you read labels like a doctor!" I smile and say, "I remember the key words." We put everything back in the red box.
text.summary: Leo visits Mia's home. Mia reads the labels on a bandage box, a bottle of medicine, and a bracelet, and she learns to ask a grown-up before she uses medicine.
